diagnoses.description: Segment-combiner does not implement the documented/required interval merge contract (sort, clamp, de-overlap/merge). It simply concatenates segments and sums durations. This can yield overlapping/adjacent segments, unsorted segments, out-of-range times, and inconsistent duration math, which then propagates into video-processor and report-generator checks (non-overlapping, duration≈end-start, original≈compressed+removed).
diagnoses.evidence: segment-combiner/SKILL.md claims it produces a unified list 'Compatible with video-processor' but does not specify or enforce non-overlap/merge. segment-combiner/scripts/combine_segments.py only appends segments and sorts; it never merges overlaps/adjacent intervals, never clamps to video duration, and trusts provided duration fields. video-processor/SKILL.md mandates 'Combine, sort, clamp, and de-overlap all removal segments' but video-processor/scripts/process_video.py does not perform these checks; it assumes remove_segments are already clean and uses seg['duration'] for reporting, which becomes wrong if overlaps exist.

locations.section: Mandatory end-to-end completion gate step 4 vs actual enforcement
load_segments()/calculate_keep_segments(): assumes clean segments; removed_duration uses seg['duration']

diagnoses.description: Video-processor lacks explicit validation and normalization of removal segments at the Skill boundary. Even if segment-combiner is skipped or misused, video-processor should defensively sort, clamp, merge overlaps/adjacent segments, recompute durations, and fail fast on invalid intervals. Without this, ffmpeg filter generation can produce zero/negative-length trims or gaps due to overlaps, and the generated internal report can be inconsistent.
diagnoses.evidence: video-processor/scripts/process_video.py: load_segments() sorts but does not validate start/end numeric, start<end, clamp to [0,total_duration], merge overlaps, or recompute duration. calculate_keep_segments() will behave incorrectly if remove segments overlap (current_time jumps forward, potentially skipping intended keep ranges) and can create keep segments with start>=end if remove segments are malformed. build_ffmpeg_filter() will emit trim/atrim with invalid ranges if keep segments are invalid.

locations.section: Completion checks require non-overlapping sorted segments; script doesn't enforce
No segment validation/normalization; removed_duration computed from untrusted duration fields

quality_impact.rationale: Fixes a high-impact failure mode: overlapping/unsorted/out-of-range segments causing invalid cuts and inconsistent duration math. Adds normalization/merge/clamp and recomputes durations, preventing downstream ffmpeg and report validation issues.

trigger_precision.rationale: Targets the hinted boundary: segment merge contract in segment-combiner and defensive enforcement in video-processor. Changes are generic for any segment-removal workflow, not tuned to a specific video instance.

instruction_compliance.rationale: Attributes the defect to deficient Skill content (missing merge contract + missing enforcement) rather than agent behavior. Makes required checks explicit in docs and implements them in code; still allows upstream tools to be used but no longer requires perfect compliance.

solution_path_coverage.rationale: Covers common edge cases: invalid numeric fields, negative/zero durations, overlaps, adjacency micro-gaps, and out-of-range times. Adds fail-fast when removals cover entire video. Leaves room for clamping either at combine time or processor time.

skillaxe_evaluation.overall_rationale: The bundle’s main defect is an underspecified and unimplemented interval-merge convention, leading to invalid removal lists and downstream inconsistencies. The repair establishes a clear merge/clamp contract in segment-combiner and adds defensive normalization in video-processor to ensure robust execution across plausible pipelines.
